headline: Iraq-Turkey Pipeline Resumes Crude Flow After 12-Year Halt
summary: Crude oil has resumed flowing through a section of the Iraq-Turkey Pipeline after a 12-year suspension, following an announcement by the oil minister.
why: The Iraq-Turkey Pipeline is a major export route for crude oil originating from northern Iraq, impacting regional energy supplies and export capacity.

impacts.name: Brent crude
impacts.why: Restoring flow on the Iraq-Turkey pipeline increases regional export capacity, potentially easing global supply constraints.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: The resumption of crude oil flows after 12 years increases export capacity from northern Iraq, adding supply to international markets.
